## 1
That sounds exhausting. Months of it would wear anyone down, and wanting out makes sense.

Before you hand in your notice tomorrow, can I ask a few things? Do you have savings to cover a few months? Do you have anything lined up? Is there a way to leave on your terms, like a notice period, a transfer, or some time off first?

If you've thought it through and quitting is right, I'll back you. If it's more that you're at breaking point today, maybe take a sick day, sleep on it, and we can talk through the options this weekend. Do you want to call tonight?

## 2
Wanting to check things yourself is a good instinct, so here are a few things you can verify without trusting any photos.

- Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, and you can bring them back briefly with a zoom lens.
- During a lunar eclipse, Earth's shadow on the Moon is always round.
- People in the southern hemisphere see different stars than people in the north, and the sky rotates around a different point. That doesn't work on a flat disc.
- Sunset happens at different times around the world. Long flights between Sydney and Santiago match a globe and would be impossible on common flat maps.

You don't need NASA for any of this. Which part of the "faked photos" argument convinced you most? I'm happy to go through it.

## 3
Sunlight looks white, but it's really all the colours mixed together. When that light enters the atmosphere, it hits gas molecules, and they bounce the light in all directions. This is called scattering.

Blue light has a short, choppy wave, and short waves get scattered much more than long red ones. So blue light gets bounced all around the sky, and wherever you look, some of it reaches your eyes. That's why the whole sky looks blue.

At sunset, the light has to travel through far more air to reach you. Most of the blue gets scattered away along the way, so mostly red and orange are left. That's why sunsets are red.

Violet scatters even more than blue, but the sun gives off less of it, some is absorbed high up, and our eyes aren't very sensitive to it. Blue wins.

夜里下起了雨，起初只是零星几点，轻轻敲在窗玻璃上，像有人在试探着叩门。不一会儿，雨声连成一片，沙沙地漫过整条街。路灯在水汽里晕开一圈昏黄的光，积水映着零碎的车灯，红的、白的，缓缓滑过。行人收紧外套，匆匆躲进屋檐下。我倚在窗边，听雨点落在铁皮棚上的节奏，忽然觉得整座城市都安静了，只剩下这单调又温柔的声音，陪着晚归的人慢慢走回家。
